target.title: fix(skills): keep command spec descriptions UTF-16 safe at the truncation cut
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill and Claude-bundle command descriptions are capped at 100 UTF-16 code units. The previous raw `slice(0, 99)` could cut between an astral character's surrogate halves, leaving malformed text immediately before the ellipsis.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both command sources now use one local truncation path backed by `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. The maintainer fixup also replaces the original false-positive assertions with exact output checks and gives the bundle branch its own bundle-command fixture.

## User Impact

Descriptions containing emoji or other supplementary-plane characters truncate cleanly in slash-command/help surfaces instead of carrying a dangling surrogate.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `443d69fe78aa54147d5050c99c6750b4114e118e`
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox `cbx_31be79e24255`, run `run_b28a24a43fd2`: `pnpm test src/skills/discovery/command-specs.test.ts` passed all 3 tests.
- The workspace regression asserts the exact 98-ASCII-plus-ellipsis result when an emoji straddles the cut.
- The bundle regression injects a real bundle command and asserts its description, prompt template, and command identity.
- Fresh AutoReview against current `origin/main`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Scope

No command-name, discovery, eligibility, prompt-template, plugin activation, configuration, or public API behavior changes. The only runtime change is surrogate-safe description truncation at the existing limit.
